en.askTitle: Change the boxes to your own budget and kitchen, and get the same priced, safety-checked meal-prep week
en.runTitle: Manchester student on £45 a week: a 7-day vegetarian plan at about 120 g protein a day

fields.label: Protein and energy goals
fields.value: About 120 g protein and about 2,600 kcal a day

fields.value: Vegetarian; I eat eggs and dairy

en.template: Help me adapt this vegetarian meal-prep week for {budget}, {goals}, {foods}, {shops}, {space} and {cooktime}. Separate whole-pack cash from food used, keep safe cooling and storage deadlines visible, and flag prices and nutrition assumptions I should check. Do not buy anything or contact anyone.

phases.title: Check public Tesco and Aldi prices, nutrition labels and official food-safety advice
phases.note: Ten staples at Tesco, the rest at Aldi, plus cooling, freezing and reheating rules
phases.judgment: The Tesco researcher noticed that the rice label’s nutrition table is for cooked rice, not the dry grains in the pack. It converted to a per-dry-weight figure and marked that number as derived, not printed on the pack.

phases.title: Build the meal plan and a self-recalculating workbook, then check it independently
phases.note: Shopping list, daily protein and calories, two batch recipes, storage plan
phases.judgment: The independent reviewer recomputed everything on their own: the £23.65 shop (Tesco £18.16 plus Aldi £5.49) and 123–128 g protein a day all matched. They also caught that the workbook still showed an averaged daily cost, which was fixed, and would not call storage settled until the yoghurt’s opened-life label and freezer-drawer fit were checked.

phases.title: Build the web page and source list, then test desktop and phone layouts
phases.judgment: The final page says plainly what stays unconfirmed: January prices and whether the frozen sauces and bread actually fit the small freezer drawer. It advises leaving about 4–5 L of clear space.

workers: Checked Tesco’s public prices and label nutrition for ten staples such as oats, milk, eggs, bread and yoghurt, and saved the storage wording for yoghurt, cheddar and long-life milk
Checked Aldi’s public prices and nutrition for lentils, pasta, tinned tomatoes, beans, vegetables, curry powder and tofu, and worked out whether protein powder is worth it
Recomputed the meal plan, shopping total and workbook from scratch, and checked whether the fridge and freezer plan is practical
